candidates.text: The suability of a State without its consent was a thing unknown to the law.
candidates.speaker: Bradley, for the Court
phrases: suability of a State without its consent was a thing unknown to the law

candidates.text: Can we suppose that, when the Eleventh Amendment was adopted, it was understood to be left open for citizens of a State to sue their own state in the federal courts
candidates.speaker: Bradley, for the Court
phrases: The supposition that it would is almost an absurdity on its face
whilst the idea of suits by citizens of other states, or of foreign states, was indignantly repelled

candidates.text: While the State cannot be compelled by suit to perform its contracts, any attempt on its part to violate property or rights acquired under its contracts may be judicially resisted
candidates.speaker: Bradley, for the Court
phrases: any attempt on its part to violate property or rights acquired under its contracts may be judicially resisted

candidates.text: It is inherent in the nature of sovereignty not to be amenable to the suit of an individual without its consent
candidates.speaker: Bradley, quoting Hamilton, Federalist No. 81
candidates.notes: Not counted: Hamilton's words predate the case, so citation counts would not measure Hans.
